text:
Today (March 2026), I had the opportunity to visit the Kanchanapisek Medical Center for dental care.

If I remember correctly, my first visit was about 8 years ago, and I've returned periodically since then. Time has passed, and it seems the place is constantly developing. This time, I noticed a new building under construction in front of the center 🏥. It seems the area is expanding.

One thing that remains the same is that the place is quite spacious, well-organized, and clean. There's also plenty of parking space 🛻🛵🚙🚗🏍️. If you park far from the building, there's a shuttle service to take you back to the parking lot, making it convenient for those who need to use the services.

After finishing my errands, I had a little time, so I walked around the ground floor. That's when I noticed there are many restaurants and cafes. I enjoyed browsing so much that I almost lost track of time.

There was one shop that made me laugh at myself a little. At first glance, I mistook the sign for a gold shop, Hua Seng Heng, but upon closer inspection, I realized it was Hua Seng Hong, a Chinese restaurant selling dim sum and steamed buns, as the red sign is very similar.

There are also snack shops like Auntie Anne's and several other restaurants, making the downstairs area quite lively. Browsing around was quite enjoyable and helped pass the waiting time.
🌽🍌🍋🍐🍊🥝🥑🍝🥙🌯🍛🥗🍡🍧🍨🍭🧁☕🧋🍯🍎🍒🍓🍉

Overall, I felt this medical center was spacious, well-organized, and offered many amenities, including parking, shuttle service, and restaurants, making the visit less stressful. But there are also areas where you can take a break or grab something to eat during the day.

December 25, 2025. Record this! Arrived at the parking lot at 9:00 AM and finally found a spot at 10:00 AM. Circled almost a hundred times, no luck at all. Drove 5-6 kilometers in the parking lot. Today was insane!

People were blocking parking spaces, waiting for cars to leave. Some got kicked out, some weren't. It's a total standard!

The parking spaces for hospital staff were also blocked, preventing further circling. When a car wanted to leave from a space near the hospital staff area, they had to circle all the way to the front entrance, which was far and time-consuming. By the time they got there, someone else had already taken it (and this happened many times today). Today was the most frustrating day I've ever driven around looking for parking in my life.

If they have the budget, they should pave the front and supplementary parking areas. The potholes are like driving off-road!

text: I've brought my child here for treatment several times. I only recently found out that the treatment is free because she's studying engineering here. Tuition averages over 200,000 baht per year because it's an international program. Today, I came for emergency treatment for a serious gynecological issue, something I only experience a few times a year. This is only the second time. The previous time, even though we were delayed in entering the treatment room, I was more impressed with the speed of treatment compared to this time. However, it seemed less professional, which I understand because the staff isn't the same as before; individual qualities vary. The positive aspect is that this crisis allowed me to turn it into an opportunity to teach my child that graduating from here means having a professional spirit befitting the educational institution that provided them with knowledge and saved their life. Wherever we work, the quality of our work reflects on the institution we attended. The most commendable thing here is the interpreter and patient reception staff. Upon arrival, the receptionist made me feel relieved that my child was saved; their demeanor and communication were excellent. If it weren't for the quality of service, I would have immediately gone to a private clinic and would have been furious on social media. I understand now why my wife kept complaining all the way home – the problem was the lack of service, specifically that the service provider wasn't the same person. When paying for medication, they didn't have the student identification documents, and it took a lot of effort to get them. Last time, the paperwork was handled from the start, but it was such a hassle to get home. As a student, my ID card wasn't enough; I needed all sorts of other certifications. And for students paying hundreds of thousands of baht in tuition annually, it's no wonder my wife was so upset. She said next time we'd go to a private institution. I told her it's just a matter of individual service quality. Even in private institutions, you can't escape it; there are always people with lower quality workmanship everywhere. Every organization has its share of people who got their jobs through connections. Today was just bad luck to encounter someone like that. That's all. What needs fixing, but isn't easy to solve today, is the lack of parking spaces. The chaos is evident. The problem is that our country has too many private car owners; they're like an unwanted burden on society. For me, I don't want to demand too much. Considering everything they've done so far, this place has passed with flying colors. Even with such complex services, it's still impressive.
